2804 discoveries from 2020 to 2026

About AI discoveries in medicine

This selection contains 2804 catalog entries dated 1 Jan 2020 to 25 Nov 2026. 2804 include structured evidence annotations describing reported tests, the AI contribution and remaining limits. Missing annotations mean those details have not been structured here, not that a study lacks evidence.

Dates follow the catalog publication policy. Coverage is selected and incomplete; entries can overlap or describe several results. Counts do not measure independent discoveries, clinical benefit or worldwide research output. Read the selection and evidence policy or compare catalog coverage by year and field.

Discoveries

25 Nov 2026Johns Hopkins University; Johns Hopkins School of Medicine

Deep learning predicts DNA damage response protein levels from routine slides

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Gated attention-based multiple-instance learning on frozen pathology foundation-model tile embeddings predicted reverse-phase protein array pathway scores from 1,673 TCGA haematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide images covering 1,527 patients with breast, endometrial, cervical and ovarian cancer and uterine carcinosarcoma. For the 11-protein DNA damage composite the out-of-fold Spearman correlation was 0.43 against 0.31 for a cancer-type-mean baseline, about 0.29-0.30 within cancer type, and at most 0.00 with shuffled targets. Cross-validation was cancer-type-stratified and site-grouped. This is a moderate retrospective association in one public cohort: there is no external validation, no clinical or treatment-response outcome, and the authors list separating the signal from proliferation as future work, noting the cell-cycle score was predicted more strongly.

Technology: Gated attention-based multiple-instance learning over frozen UNI2-h and Virchow2 tile embeddings jointly regresses six RPPA pathway scores.

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Preprint Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The attention-based model predicts DNA damage response protein scores from slide-tile embeddings.
Test and result
Five-fold cancer-type-stratified, site-grouped cross-validation against measured RPPA values, compared with a cancer-type-mean baseline and a shuffled-target control.
Limitation / still unknown
No external cohort; no clinical or therapy-response outcome; the signal is not separated from proliferation; within-type correlation is moderate; not peer reviewed.

24 Nov 2026University Medical Center Utrecht; Meta VCI Map consortium; Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf; Research Centre Jülich

Learned lesion-network models identify shared and specific stroke cognition patterns

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A November 24, 2026 preprint analyzed 3,034 patients across 13 stroke cohorts using learned models of lesion anatomy, network connectivity and clinical characteristics. Structural lesion connectivity supplied most of the gain beyond clinical information and infarct size, with left anterior thalamic connectivity consistently informative across cognitive outcomes. Benefits persisted for several outcomes when entire cohorts were held out. The results support a bounded lesion-in-context account of cognitive impairment, without establishing causal circuitry or clinical readiness.

Technology: Stacked ridge classifiers and regularized logistic meta-learner; interpretable feature ablation and cross-cohort prediction

Editorial relevance 53 medicine PreprintPreprint Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Ridge base classifiers learned complementary lesion representations and a logistic stacking model combined out-of-fold predictions. Ablation, stable coefficients and unseen-cohort tests linked predictive gains to specific network anatomy rather than lesion volume alone.
Test and result
Nested repeated cross-validation evaluated 3,034 patients from 13 cohorts. Adding anatomy and connectivity improved six of seven targets; any-domain impairment AUPRC rose from 0.67 to 0.71. Leave-one-cohort-out tests retained significant gains for three of seven targets by normalized AUPRC. Stable model coefficients highlighted shared thalamic connectivity and domain-specific anatomical profiles.
Limitation / still unknown
Retrospective pooled cohorts were heterogeneous and predominantly represented mild strokes and Asian or European ancestry. Cognitive outcomes were binary at one assessment within a year, with premorbid cognition unavailable. Cross-cohort performance varied and several domain gains did not transfer significantly. Prediction and coefficient stability do not prove causation or clinical utility.

24 Nov 2026Shahid Bahonar University of Kerman; University of Saskatchewan; Sport Science Research Institute

Machine learning links multidomain profiles to fall history

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In a cross-sectional study of 147 community-dwelling adults aged 55 and older, machine-learning models classified ordered past-year fall-history groups from physical-function, activity, health and social measures. Random Forest reported four-class accuracy of 0.946 and binary AUC of 0.968 under internal five-fold validation after excluding fall-location, fall-situation and fear-of-falling variables. The preprint describes associations with recorded fall history, not prediction of future falls. A small, imbalanced single-region sample and self-reported measures limit generalization; external and prospective validation remain necessary.

Technology: Random Forest, logistic regression, gradient boosting and SVM learn multidomain associations with past-year fall-history strata; feature importance characterizes the internally evaluated profile.

Editorial relevance 40 medicine PreprintPreprint Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Random Forest, logistic regression, gradient boosting and SVM learn multidomain associations with past-year fall-history strata; feature importance characterizes the internally evaluated profile.
Test and result
Stratified five-fold internal classification of fall-history strata in 147 adults, excluding specified post-fall variables.
Limitation / still unknown
Cross-sectional history, self-report and small uneven strata; no external validation, causal effects or demonstrated future-fall prediction.

24 Nov 2026Jinggangshan University; The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Shenzhen University of Advanced Technology; Shenzhen People’s Hospital

Unsupervised program learning links a beta-cell signature to insulin secretion

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A November 24, 2026 preprint used donor-resolved non-negative matrix factorization and consensus program discovery to identify a beta-cell gene program reduced in type 2 diabetes. Learned program definitions were fixed before testing in other datasets. Higher program scores were associated with greater stimulated insulin release in donor-matched measurements from two laboratories. The laboratories shared most donors, so these are complementary measurements rather than independent biological replications, and the association does not establish a causal mechanism or treatment target.

Technology: Donor-resolved non-smooth non-negative matrix factorization; cross-donor consensus gene-program discovery

Editorial relevance 47 medicine PreprintPreprint Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
NMF learned additive gene-expression programs separately in donor/cell-type units; cross-donor consensus construction identified recurring programs before outcome testing. This learned program discovery, rather than visualization or dimensionality reduction alone, enabled the fixed beta-cell signature and its subsequent functional association tests.
Test and result
Program discovery used 48 donors. Primary independent single-cell validation used 55 eligible HPAP donors, with additional pooled Smart-seq2 and bulk analyses. Functional associations used 52 UPenn and 42 Vanderbilt donors, of whom 39 overlapped; higher frozen program scores tracked stimulated insulin release after diagnosis and preparation-quality adjustments.
Limitation / still unknown
Existing-data associations are retrospective and do not establish that the program causes secretory dysfunction. Two laboratories largely measured the same donors; bulk cell-composition adjustment was not robust across platforms. Patient-level clinical utility, causal perturbation and independent biological replication remain unestablished.

24 Nov 2026University Hospital Erlangen; Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg; iThera Medical GmbH; Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg

AI-segmented imaging localizes pigmentation bias in oximetry

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A pretrained convolutional network separated tissue compartments in an optoacoustic imaging study of 46 healthy volunteers spanning six Fitzpatrick skin types. Across 3,016 scans and 41 wavelengths, superficial skin signals showed stronger pigmentation associations and unreliable oxygenation responses, while deeper muscle signals responded more clearly to physiological challenges. This preprint characterizes tissue- and wavelength-dependent optoacoustic measurements; it does not directly quantify pulse-oximeter error, validate oxygen saturation against an independent reference or demonstrate clinical benefit.

Technology: A convolutional neural network trained on independently annotated ultrasound data segments skin, adipose tissue, fascia and muscle, enabling compartment-specific optoacoustic spectral and oxygenation analysis.

Editorial relevance 60 medicine PreprintPreprint Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
A convolutional neural network trained on independently annotated ultrasound data segments skin, adipose tissue, fascia and muscle, enabling compartment-specific optoacoustic spectral and oxygenation analysis.
Test and result
Single-center physiological imaging study in 46 volunteers, with compartment-resolved spectra and responses during oxygenation challenges.
Limitation / still unknown
No independent oxygen-saturation reference; unequal groups, coarse pigmentation classification and single anatomical region/system limit generalization; no direct pulse-oximeter validation.

24 Nov 2026Fujian Medical University Union Hospital

Survival learning prioritizes cohort-specific NFKB1 associations in colorectal cancer

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A study used penalized Cox models and CoxBoost to prioritize NFKB1 for retrospective colorectal-cancer survival analysis. Higher expression was associated with favorable survival in selected external cohorts, but the adjusted association was not significant in TCGA-COAD. Model discrimination was modest: the best overall mean time-dependent AUC was 0.650. A separate spatial analysis used one tissue specimen and does not establish macrophage-specific causality. NFKB1 remains an exploratory association, without a validated clinical cutoff or demonstrated treatment benefit.

Technology: LASSO-Cox, ridge/elastic-net Cox and CoxBoost survival learning

AI contribution
Learned survival models prioritize genes for prognostic association analysis; language assistants did not conduct scientific analysis.
Test and result
Existing TCGA development data and separate GEO cohort survival associations; heterogeneous endpoints and moderate discrimination.
Limitation / still unknown
Association is not uniformly significant across cohorts or causal; one spatial specimen and exploratory protein-image comparisons constrain interpretation. Drug-response estimates are predictions.

24 Nov 2026China-Japan Union Hospital of Jilin University, Jilin University

Machine learning derives an exploratory two-gene signature in gastric cancer

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Differential expression and summary-data-based Mendelian randomization on TCGA gastric cancer data prioritized 24 heat-shock-protein-associated genes, consensus clustering defined two molecular clusters, and LASSO-Cox regression derived an exploratory F7-PRNP prognostic signature. siRNA knockdown of F7 or PRNP inhibited proliferation, migration and invasion in HGC27 and AGS cells. The authors state that derivation and evaluation used the same TCGA cohort, so the performance estimates are likely optimistic and independent validation is required; compound prioritization, docking and molecular dynamics are computational only.

Technology: LASSO-Cox regression selects the prognostic genes from TCGA transcriptomes; oncoPredict models trained on GDSC2 cell-line data prioritize compounds in silico.

24 Nov 2026Seventh People's Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Changhai Hospital, Naval Medical University

Machine learning selects an exploratory senescence-related gene score in PMOS

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Using two public ovarian-cell datasets (13 PMOS and 9 control samples), univariate logistic regression, SVM-RFE and LASSO selected a five-gene SASP-related score (DYNLRB2, MMP9, A1BG, PGD, APLP2) with apparent AUC 0.991 on the development data and AUC 0.838 in an exploratory skeletal-muscle dataset (10 versus 13 samples). The authors state the apparent AUC should not be interpreted as evidence of diagnostic ability: dataset origin is confounded with cell type, the muscle dataset is not tissue-matched, no individual gene there remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and virtual screening against MMP9 is unvalidated. Technology: Logistic regression, SVM-RFE and LASSO select a five-gene score from public transcriptomes; DrugCLIP screens compounds against MMP9 in silico.

24 Nov 2026Shuguang Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Shanghai Academy of Traditional Chinese Medicine

Machine learning prioritises osteoarthritis genes tested under macrophage stretch

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Random forest ranking and LASSO regression narrowed a 168-gene synovial co-expression module to five candidates (E2F3, C6orf211, NDUFC2, SPCS2, DOCK10) using public datasets (discovery 29 normal and 30 osteoarthritis samples; auxiliary GSE89408 with 28 and 22). The combined score reached AUC 0.817 in discovery and 0.797 in the auxiliary cohort. In LPS-activated RAW264.7 macrophages (six biological replicates per group), cyclic stretch lowered E2F3, SPCS2 and DOCK10 and raised NDUFC2 relative to LPS alone, alongside lower inflammatory readouts. The authors note the auxiliary cohort also informed selection and is not independent validation, the sample is small, the cell line is murine, there was no stretch-only or time-course control, and the LPS-induced E2F3 protein increase was not significant.

Technology: Random forest importance ranking and LASSO regression select candidate genes from a WGCNA co-expression module; ridge logistic regression with bootstrap replicates estimates optimism.

Limitation / still unknown
No independent human validation cohort; no causal evidence; murine cell line only; no stretch-only or time-course control; weak module-to-macrophage association.

24 Nov 2026Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center; Sun Yat-sen University School of Computer Science and Engineering; Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center

Deep learning scores Claudin18.2 staining in gastric cancer slides across clones

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A pipeline that scores Claudin18.2 immunohistochemistry on whole-slide images used a LoRA-adapted UNI pathology foundation model for tumour recognition, adapter-based staining-intensity classification and two rounds of active learning. Agreement with pathologist-consensus 2/3+ scoring was ICC 0.849 on 195 internal test slides and 0.894 on 135 prospectively collected slides, and ICC 0.792-0.827 for three other antibody clones tested without retraining. In a non-randomised reader study, AI assistance improved every pathologist's agreement with the reference standard and shortened review time. The authors state the study is single-centre with limited prospective and cross-clone cohorts, uses expert consensus rather than absolute ground truth, may propagate errors across modules, and provides no treatment-response or outcome data; at the 50% cutoff the retrospective AUC was lower than one pathologist's.

Technology: UNI pathology foundation model (ViT-L/16) adapted with LoRA and inserted adapters, plus active learning, for tumour recognition and staining-intensity scoring.

Editorial relevance 60 medicine Published article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Foundation-model-based tumour recognition and staining-intensity modules produce the slide-level Claudin18.2 score.
Test and result
Slide-level agreement with pathologist consensus on 195 internal test slides and 135 prospectively collected slides, cross-clone evaluation of three further antibody clones, and a six-pathologist reader study.
Limitation / still unknown
Single centre; limited prospective and cross-clone cohorts; reader study not randomised; no therapy-response or outcome data; the paper does not state whether the model was frozen before prospective enrolment, so this is treated as evaluation on collected slides rather than prospective workflow use.

24 Nov 2026Seoul National University

Deep learning EEG metric linked to mortality in obstructive sleep apnea

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A deep-learning model trained on 22,044 polysomnography recordings estimated the apnea-hypopnea index from a single EEG channel, correlating r=0.88 with the scored index in internal testing and r=0.50 to 0.62 in three external test sets. Two derived metrics, the discrepancy between the EEG-based and scored index and an estimate from epochs without scored respiratory events, were associated with all-cause and non-cardiovascular mortality among participants free of cardiovascular disease after adjustment for the apnea-hypopnea index and clinical risk factors; the event-free estimate was also associated with cardiovascular mortality in the highest versus lowest quartile. Data came from the KISS, MESA, MrOS and SHHS cohorts. The findings are retrospective associations in a preprint, external agreement is weaker, hazard ratios and per-cohort sizes were not reviewed, and the authors suggest the discrepancy is not solely model error.

Technology: Deep-learning model estimates the apnea-hypopnea index from a single EEG channel; derived discrepancy metrics are tested against mortality.

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Preprint Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The deep-learning model produces the EEG-based index whose discrepancy from the scored index is the tested metric.
Test and result
Internal and three external test sets for index estimation, then retrospective cohort association of the derived metrics with mortality after adjustment for the apnea-hypopnea index and clinical risk factors.
Limitation / still unknown
Weaker external agreement; no causal or clinical-utility evidence; hazard ratios, covariate list, follow-up and per-cohort sizes not reviewed; not peer reviewed; one author holds related patents and leads a company.

23 Nov 2026EPFL; University Hospital Zurich; University of Zurich; University of Bern

Multimodal AI finds lung-cancer tissue signatures associated with survival

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A November 23, 2026 preprint reports that VirTues-M2 learned joint tissue morphology and spatial-protein representations to discover survival-associated cellular signatures in lung cancer. Signatures selected on 737 patients stratified survival in 316 held-out patients and transferred without retraining to a separate 39-patient cohort. Low-risk signatures marked organized immune-rich neighborhoods; high-risk signatures marked more disorganized tumor-rich tissue. These are retrospective prognostic associations with small external validation and no demonstrated treatment benefit.

Technology: VirTues-M2; multimodal vision transformer and learned cell-signature transfer

Editorial relevance 53 medicine PreprintPreprint Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
A marker-aware multimodal transformer learned joint H&E and spatial-proteomics representations. Clustering enabled annotation-free cell-state discovery; Cox screening selected survival-linked populations and random-forest classifiers transferred their membership to another cohort.
Test and result
Signature selection used 737 discovery patients and evaluation used 316 held-out patients. Combined signatures reached C-index 0.646 and hazard ratio 3.09 in the test set. Unchanged signature classifiers transferred to 39 external patients; combined signatures had C-index 0.636 and hazard ratio 2.87 (p=0.039).
Limitation / still unknown
Retrospective survival associations do not establish causation or treatment-response prediction. External validation is small; the H&E-only external signature was not significant at p<0.05. Test patients used pre-specified tertiles, whereas external patients used a median split. Prospective clinical utility and robustness require further evaluation.

23 Nov 2026Balgrist University Hospital; University of Zurich

Learned MRI models link cord motion and compression level to myelopathy severity

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A November 23, 2026 study analyzed MRI measurements from 112 patients with degenerative cervical myelopathy. Learned hierarchical classifiers identified compression at C3/4 as a severity-associated feature. In the larger training subgroup with compression elsewhere, adding spinal cord motion improved cross-validated severity classification accuracy from 69.6% to 73.7%. Internal testing on 22 patients produced one additional correct classification. Test and result
A 90-patient training set and 22-patient internal test set were formed from 112 patients. In the 75-patient training subgroup without maximum compression at C3/4, adding motion improved repeated cross-validated accuracy from 69.6% to 73.7% (p=0.0059); the final internal test comparison gained one correct classification.
Limitation / still unknown
A small, single-center and imbalanced cohort with data-driven model selection remains vulnerable to overfitting. The 15-patient C3/4 training subgroup was too small for the motion-feature comparison. The study reports no external validation or clinical-impact evaluation; performance beyond this held-out single-center cohort is unknown.

Aggregate Accuracy Hides Diagnosis-Specific Failure in Medical Vision-Language Models

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: On 6,048 balanced ChestX-ray14 cases, HuatuoGPT-Vision and Qwen2.5-VL detected none of 432 pneumothorax-positive cases; comparison models detected 38% and 67%. This model-specific failure also appeared at larger model scale. The failure replicated on an independent SIIM-ACR set with radiologist-drawn masks: the same models detected 0/432 confirmed pneumothoraces, including 0/144 largest lesions. Retrospective diagnostic evaluation only; no clinical benefit established.

Technology: Medical vision-language models directly answered per-finding questions from chest radiographs; the study evaluated their diagnosis-specific recall, confidence and internal representations.

11 Nov 2026University of Calgary

Deep learning brain age from routine CT is linked to stroke outcome

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In 1,173 acute ischemic stroke patients from a prospective multicenter cohort, a deep learning model estimated brain age from contralesional baseline non-contrast CT. Brain age gap was higher in patients than in controls (+3.1 +/- 9.1 years) and higher gap was associated with worse 90-day functional status after adjustment (proportional odds ratio 1.091 per 5 years; 95% CI 1.023 to 1.162; p=0.008). It added only modest discrimination, and the authors call for external validation.
